author: J. D. Beck
title: UCLA baseball defeats Maryland 12-2 in series opener at Jackie Robinson Stadium
text:
The UCLA baseball team defeated Maryland 12-2 on Mar. 20 in the opening game of their series at Jackie Robinson Stadium.
The win keeps the Bruins ranked No. 1 and improves their record to 19-2 overall and 7-0 in Big Ten play. The game was decided by a six-run seventh inning, which pushed the margin to ten runs and resulted in UCLA’s fifth run-rule victory of the season.
Eight out of nine starters for UCLA recorded hits, with Cashel Dugger hitting a grand slam in the first inning—his second of the year—and finishing with two hits. Payton Brennan, Dominic Cadiz, and Phoenix Call also had two hits each. Roch Cholowsky contributed with two runs batted in and scored twice, while Dean West reached base three times and drove in two runs after being hit by pitches with the bases loaded. The Bruins were hit by pitches eight times during the game.
Starting pitcher Logan Reddemann improved his record to 6-0 after striking out seven batters, walking one, and allowing two earned runs over eight hits. The Bruins took an early lead with five runs in the first inning, highlighted by Dugger’s grand slam. Maryland managed to score single runs in both the third and sixth innings but could not keep up with UCLA’s offense.
Reliever Ian May pitched a scoreless seventh inning before UCLA sealed the win with another offensive surge. The game ended after seven innings due to the run rule.
UCLA will continue its series against Maryland at Jackie Robinson Stadium tomorrow at 2 p.m., with live coverage available on B1G+.
